title: 14-Year-Old Swimmer Zooms Past Records Like a Dolphin on Turbo Boost!
summary: Have you ever tried to swim four different strokes in one race without stopping? It's called the individual medley, or IM, and it's super tough. Now imagine doing it so fast that you become one of the best 14-year-olds in history! That's exactly what Lauren Lonsdale did at a big swim meet in Sacramento. She zoomed through the 400-meter IM in 4 minutes and 44 seconds. That's like swimming the length of four football fields using butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle—and she did it faster than almost anyone her age ever has! She's now the 4th-fastest 13-14 girl in U.S. history for that event. But wait, there's more! Right after that exhausting race, Lauren jumped back in the pool and won the 100-meter backstroke in 1:01.77. That's just a blink slower than her personal best. She must have superhero stamina! Another 14-year-old star, Natalia Lesniewska, also made waves. She won the 100-meter freestyle in 55.88 seconds, tying for 10th all-time in her age group. That's like racing a speedy motorboat! On the boys' side, Nathan Foucu broke the 50-second barrier in the 100 free for the first time, touching in 49.94. And brothers Lupo and Vito Sgroi finished 1-2 in the 400 IM, with Lupo crushing his old best by over 5 seconds. These young swimmers are proving that age is just a number when you have talent and determination!
why_it_matters: These swimmers prove that with hard work and believing in yourself, you can reach goals that seem out of reach — just like learning a new skill at school or in sports.

USA Swimming (the national organization that runs competitive swimming in America) keeps careful records for each age group, and being in the top 10 all‑time is a huge honor.
In swimming, breaking a ‘barrier’ like the 50‑second mark in the 100 freestyle often means a whole new level of speed has been reached.
Article_Structure: WHO: Young swimmers Lauren Lonsdale, Natalia Lesniewska, Nathan Foucu, and brothers Lupo and Vito Sgroi.
WHAT: Lauren Lonsdale became the 4th‑fastest 13‑14 girl in U.S. history in the 400m IM (4:44), won the 100m backstroke, and others set fast times.

WHY: Their talent and determination showed that age doesn’t stop you from swimming incredibly fast.

perspectives.description: Coaches see Lauren as a future star who could one day represent the country at the Olympics, inspired by her amazing stamina.
Some parents worry that focusing on records at such a young age might put too much pressure on kids and take the fun out of swimming.
Swimming officials note that age‑group records are broken frequently as training methods improve, so these marks might not stand forever.
